chunks: From him, from Abu Ali al-Wasiti, from al-Husayn ibn Aban, from the one who mentioned, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

If a man were to love a man for the Sake of Allah, Allah would Reward him upon his love for him, and even if it was so that the beloved was from the people of the Fire in the Knowledge of Allah; and if a man were to hate a man for the Sake of Allah, Allah would Reward him upon his hatred for him, and even if it was so that the hated one was from the people of the Paradise in the Knowledge of Allah.

key_terms.لِلَّهِ: For the Sake of Allah (sincerity of intention)

ai.seo_question: Does the spiritual status of the person determine the reward for loving them for Allah's sake?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the principle of *al-hubb wa al-bughd li-lahi* (love and hatred for God’s sake), emphasizing that the spiritual merit lies in the sincerity of the act rather than the intrinsic status of the object. It highlights a key Shia theological nuance: one can love a person destined for Hell if the love is rooted in their divine attributes or obedience, and hate a person destined for Paradise if the hatred stems from their specific sins or opposition to truth. This distinction underscores that *hubb* and *bukhd* are acts of worship when directed for God's pleasure, independent of the beloved's final eschatological fate.
